conditions: reference; coupled; local; varying; nearby; refractory; quartic
measurement: Latent network events with a ripple component per second of rest (outside running bouts and the first and last second), after rejection; a doublet counts once; pooled over replicates
source_location: Buzsáki 2015 Fig. 3C (read from figure); Davidson et al. 2009 Results, 'Extended replay detected by neural decoding' and 'Relationship between extended replay and ripples'
rationale: Lower: ripples during immobility on a maze, about 0.13/s (figure; 0.22/s in home-cage quiet waking). Upper: multiunit candidate events during stops, 0.32-0.40/s (text). Both depend on detection thresholds, so the latent rate is compared. Sleep rates (0.3-0.5/s, Nguyen et al. 2009) are outside the reference state.

conditions: reference; coupled; local; varying; nearby; refractory; quartic
measurement: Median over ripple components of the FFT peak frequency of each rendered, noise-free, unit-amplitude ripple waveform
rationale: Caption modes of per-event peak frequency: 177 Hz in home-cage quiet waking and 187 Hz during immobility on a maze; 5 Hz each side for comparing a median with a histogram mode. The sleep mode (167 Hz) is outside the reference state.

conditions: none (state differs; reported beside the reference)
measurement: Median over ripple components of the instantaneous frequency (Hilbert phase derivative of the noise-free rendering) 7.5 ms before the envelope's peak minus 7.5 ms after it
source_location: Results, 'Dynamic frequency structure of ripple events'; Fig. 2C (read from figure); Discussion, 'Ripple frequency dynamics'
rationale: The median instantaneous-frequency trace falls about 15-20 Hz over about 15 ms around the peak (figure); 5 Hz each side for reading it. About 25% of ripples rise instead (Discussion); the model has no rising ripples, a limitation recorded in the parameter notes rather than a target.

measurement: Median over ripple components of the time channel 0's 100-250 Hz RMS (17 ms window) stays above 2 SD of the matched noise-only rendering's RMS, in the run that contains the component's centre, on rendered sessions with noise
source_location: Fig. 1B (medians read from figure; the detection convention is in the supplement, not accessed)
rationale: Medians of about 45-55 ms in familiar and novel environments (figure, log axis); 5 ms each side for reading it. The measurement uses Patel et al. 2013's RMS convention since this source's was not accessed. Local profiles, varying noise and the quartic envelope change this measurement by design and are reported, not gated.

conditions: none (state differs; reported beside the reference)
measurement: Mean over ripple components of Patel et al.'s convention: 100-250 Hz RMS in a 17 ms window above 2 SD for at least 20 ms and reaching 5 SD, bounded where it falls below 2 SD
source_location: Materials and Methods, 'Ripple event detection'; Fig. 3C (read from figure)
rationale: Session means of about 30-37 ms across amplitude classes (figure); 10% each side for reading it.

conditions: reference; coupled; local; varying; nearby; refractory; quartic
measurement: Median over sharp-wave components of the full width at 10% of peak of the noise-free radiatum deflection
rationale: 'SPWs are large amplitude negative polarity deflections (40-100 ms) in CA1 stratum radiatum'. The convention is unstated; the width at 10% of peak stands for the visible extent.

conditions: reference; coupled; local; varying; nearby; refractory; quartic
measurement: Mean over place and other pyramidal units of the realized firing rate over rest, events included
source_location: Csicsvari et al. 1999 p. 278; Mizuseki & Buzsáki 2013 Results and Fig. 1B (read from figure)
rationale: Upper: non-theta mean 1.4 +/- 0.09 Hz (SE), biased upward by excluding silent cells. Lower: the lognormal rate distribution's mode, about 0.3-0.5 Hz (figure).

conditions: reference; coupled; local; varying; nearby; refractory; quartic
measurement: Mean over interneurons of the realized firing rate over rest, events included
rationale: Non-theta means 8.3 +/- 1.02 Hz (alveus/oriens) and 14.3 +/- 1.32 Hz (pyramidal layer), mean +/- SE; bounds 2 SE beyond each.

conditions: reference; coupled; local; varying; nearby; refractory; quartic
measurement: Interneurons' pooled rate within 5 ms of the centres of the ripples of swr and ripple_doublet events, over their pooled rate at rest outside every event's network window at 10% of peak
rationale: 'Interneurons in both groups increased approximately threefold relative to the no-SPW baseline period' (p. 279), 'by only 2.5-3' (p. 284); SPW/no-SPW rate ratios 3.8 and 2.8 (p. 278). Measured on large ripples (7 SD), hence swr and doublet events only.

conditions: reference; coupled; local; varying; nearby; refractory; quartic
measurement: Place and other pyramidal units' pooled rate within 5 ms of the centres of the ripples of swr and ripple_doublet events, over their pooled rate at rest outside every event's network window at 10% of peak
rationale: 'pyramidal cells increased 6.6-fold at the peak of the SPW compared with that of no-SPW epochs' (p. 279); SPW/no-SPW rate ratio 8.6 +/- 0.44 (SE, p. 278). Measured on large ripples (7 SD), hence swr and doublet events only.

conditions: reference; coupled; local; varying; nearby; refractory; quartic
measurement: Mean over events with a ripple of the fraction of place and other pyramidal units that fire at least one spike within 25 ms of the first ripple's centre
rationale: 'On the average, approximately 10% of the recorded neurons fired in the time window of the SPW-associated fast oscillatory event (50 msec)'; a factor of two either side, since the units a probe records differ from the simulated population.

conditions: reference; coupled; local; varying; nearby; refractory; quartic
measurement: 95th percentile over events with a ripple of the same fraction
source_location: Ylinen et al. 1995 p. 35; Csicsvari et al. 2000 p. 588, Fig. 3C (read from figure)
rationale: Per-event participation ranges 0-40% (Ylinen, text); about 28% of CA1 pyramidal cells fire within 50 ms in the largest (7 SD) events (Csicsvari 2000, figure).

measurement: Pearson correlation over swr and ripple_doublet events between the first sharp wave's amplitude and the square of the first ripple's SNR
source_location: Results, 'Segregation and definition of ripple and fast gamma oscillations'
rationale: The SPW sink correlated with ripple power, r = 0.47 (0.30-0.55 by animal). Directional: the coupled condition's latent correlation, 0.6, is an assumed stress value, so only a positive correlation at least the smallest reported r is required.

conditions: reference; local; varying; nearby; refractory; quartic
rationale: The reference draws strengths independently (strength_correlation 0), an assumed control that does not reproduce the reported coupling; the bounds allow for sampling over the validation replicates.

measurement: Spearman correlation over swr and ripple_doublet events between the first sharp wave's amplitude and the first ripple's onset frequency
rationale: 'both the frequency and magnitude of fast oscillations are positively correlated with the magnitude of SPWs' (abstract). The Results describe an inverted U between them, so only the sign is required.

conditions: reference; coupled; local; varying; nearby; refractory; quartic
measurement: Median over ripple doublets and triplets of consecutive ripples' centre-to-centre interval
source_location: Results, 'Relationship between extended replay and ripples'; Fig. 5A
rationale: 8.8-11.8 ripples/s within replay events imply mean spacings of 85-114 ms (arithmetic; the source reports rates, not intervals).
